### Data 

```{r}

data <- read.csv('../sample_data/publist_orders.csv', stringsAsFactors = F)

number_pubs <- nrow(data)

```

The data used in this example is a list of `r number_pubs` pubs in Dublin, Ireland with their associated X and Y coordinates.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

if(!("pacman" %in% rownames(installed.packages()))){
  install.packages("pacman")
}

library(pacman)
p_load(tidyverse)
p_load(DT)
p_load(dplyr)
```

```{r}
data <- data %>% select(-c(pickupTime,dropoffTime, quantity)) %>% mutate(across(2:3, ~ format(round(.x, digits=5), nsmall = 5))) 

datatable(data, colnames = c("Pub Name (id)",
                           "X-Coordinate (X)",
                           "Y-Coordinate (Y)")
                           , options = list(dom = 't', scrollY = "200px", pageLength=nrow(data), columnDefs = list(list(className = 'dt-right', targets = 2:3))))

```

### Running the example

An R script with all the lines needed to run the example can be found [here](https://github.com/Icepack-co/examples/blob/master/R/nvd-1-basic.R).

The example uses the **iceR** package which will first need to be installed (see information [here](https://github.com/Icepack-co/iceR)) and then loaded, along with the gridExtra package to help with plotting the results.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
library(iceR)
library(gridExtra)

```


Execute the example as follows:

1. Create an apiHelper object with the model type you'd like to solve

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
api <- new("apiHelper", modelType = 'nvd-hap0j2y4zlm1', configFile = '../config.json')
```


2. Create the model and add some data to it

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

# Create the model
sr <- new (NVD.SolveRequest)
sr$model <- new (NVD.Model)

# Load the data
data <- read.csv('../sample_data/publist_orders.csv', stringsAsFactors = F)

# View the loaded data (if desired)
ggplot() + geom_point(data = data, aes(x = X, y = Y)) + theme_bw()

# Add some additional information to the data (this would normally be a function of the input data)
set.seed(123)
data$Frequency <- sample(x = c(4,2,1), size = nrow(data),replace = T)
data$visitTime <- round(runif(n = nrow(data), 60, 120),0)
# Assume that each visit takes somewhere between 1 and 2 hours (f you've ever been to an Irish pub, you'll know it's tough to visit for less than an hour!).

repHomeLocation <- 'My Sales Rep (@Guinness)'
data$id[1] <- repHomeLocation

```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false

# Configure the model and add the data to it

periodLength <- 20
weekLength <- 5

sr$model$configuration <- new (NVD.Configuration)
sr$model$configuration$timeUnit <- 1
sr$model$configuration$timeCoef <- 1
sr$model$configuration$timeCostCoef <- 0
sr$model$configuration$distanceUnit <- 4
sr$model$configuration$distanceCostCoef <- 1
sr$model$configuration$intraTerritoryBalance <- 1
sr$model$configuration$interTerritoryBalance <- 1
sr$model$configuration$weekLength = weekLength
sr$model$configuration$periodLength = periodLength
sr$model$configuration$toString() %>% cat

t <- new(NVD.Territory)
t$id <- repHomeLocation
t$dailyStartTime <- 0
t$dailyEndTime <- 400
t$location <- new (NVD.Geocode)
t$location$longitude <- data %>% filter(id == repHomeLocation) %>% select(X) %>% unlist()
t$location$latitude <- data %>% filter(id == repHomeLocation) %>% select(Y) %>% unlist()
t$dailyStartTime <- rep(0, periodLength)
t$dailyEndTime <- rep(440, periodLength)  # assuming a 6h40m hour work day, we don't want them overwhelmed
                                          # this can be modified quite easily on a day-to-day basis
sr$model$territories <- t

for(i in 2:nrow(data)){
  v <- new (NVD.Visit)
  s <- data[i,]
  v$id <- as.character(s$id)
  v$location <- new(NVD.Geocode)
  v$location$longitude <- s$X
  v$location$latitude <- s$Y
  v$visitTime <- s$visitTime
  v$territoryRelations <- new (NVD.Visit.TerritoryRelation)
  v$territoryRelations$type <- 0 # 0 INCLUSIVE, 1 EXCLUSIVE
  v$territoryRelations$territoryIds <- repHomeLocation

  #   SEVEN_TIMES_A_WEEK = 1; #only applicable to a 7-day week
  #   SIX_TIMES_A_WEEK = 2;   #only applicable to a 6-day week
  #   FIVE_TIMES_A_WEEK = 3;
  #   FOUR_TIMES_A_WEEK = 4;
  #   THREE_TIMES_A_WEEK = 5;
  #   TWICE_A_WEEK = 6;       # it is unusual to implement this profile as we normally want twice a week with a certain gap between days.
  #   ONCE_A_WEEK = 7;        # frequency 4 in this example
  #   EVERY_SECOND_WEEK = 8;  # frequency 2 in this example
  #   ONCE_A_MONTH = 9;       # frequency 1 in this example
  if(s$Frequency == 4){
    v$profile$frequencyType =  7;
  }else if(s$Frequency == 2){
    v$profile$frequencyType = 8
  } else if (s$Frequency <= 1){
    v$profile$frequencyType = 9;
  }else {
    stop()
  }
  sr$model$visits[[length(sr$model$visits) + 1]]<- v
}

# Set the other relevant information
sr$solveType <- 0 # 0 for optimise, 1 for evaluate, 2 for reoptimise

# View the model in plain-text format (string or JSON)
sr$model$toString() %>% cat
sr$model$toJSON() %>% cat

```

3. Submit the model to the API

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
requestID <- api %>% postSolveRequest(sr)  
```


4. Retrieve the model response

NOTE: It takes about a minute to solve
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
resp <- api %>% getResponse(requestID)
```

5. Visualise the result

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

# Tabulate the data in native-R format
tab <- resp %>% tabulate(sr) 
# You'll notice this tabulates the Pareto frontier here, since
# no solution from the frontier has been selected yet.
tab$frontier %>% head

# Plot the data (ggplot or leaflet)
resp %>% plotResponse(sr) # ggplot                       
resp %>% plotResponseLeaflet(sr) # leaflet (if it's mappable)
```
